findings.finding: Application is a monolith with no service separation, no API layer, and no cloud-native patterns (12-factor app). All logic is embedded in two ColdFusion templates.
No externalized configuration — datasource name, file paths, and session settings are hardcoded in source files.
File storage uses a local disk path (D:\docroot\files\) instead of cloud object storage (S3).
Session state is server-side and instance-bound. No distributed session store or stateless design.
No health check endpoints for load balancer integration or container orchestration probes.
Single-instance architecture with no auto-scaling, no load balancing, and no redundancy.
No Dockerfile or container configuration exists. Deployment is manual file copy to Windows IIS server.
Application depends on Adobe ColdFusion 8 runtime configured through a GUI (ColdFusion Administrator). Not containerizable without rework.
Hardcoded Windows file paths create platform dependency preventing portability to Linux containers.
No process management or graceful shutdown handling.
Datasource configuration lives in ColdFusion Administrator (external to code), requiring runtime state conflicting with immutable containers.
Application runs on proprietary Adobe ColdFusion 8 (commercial, EOL). No open-source runtime maintains compatibility.
Database is proprietary Microsoft SQL Server 2005 (commercial, EOL). Queries use basic SQL portable to open-source alternatives.
Web server is proprietary Microsoft IIS 7 on Windows Server 2008 (commercial, EOL).
Operating system is Windows Server 2008 (commercial, EOL). Migration to Linux reduces licensing costs.
Database is self-managed SQL Server 2005 (EOL April 2016) with no managed database service.
SQL queries built via string concatenation with no parameterization — SQL injection vulnerabilities in both files.
No database connection pooling, no ORM, no data access layer. Raw queries embedded in presentation templates.
No database backup strategy visible. Single instance with no replication or failover.
Database schema is simple (single documents table). Migration complexity is low from a data structure perspective.
No analytics, reporting, or data pipeline capabilities exist. Application is purely a document search and download tool.
No usage metrics collected — document access patterns, search queries, and download frequency not tracked.
Documents table contains metadata that could feed analytics if captured in a data warehouse.
No CI/CD pipeline exists. Deployment is manual file copy over network share.
No automated tests of any kind (unit, integration, end-to-end).
No infrastructure as code (no CloudFormation, Terraform, or CDK).
No application logging or monitoring. No CloudWatch integration.
No version-controlled deployment artifacts or structured release process.
No environment separation (dev/staging/production) visible.
Git repository exists with .gitignore — basic version control is in place.
No API layer for AI/ML service integration. Cannot integrate AI services without first building an API.
No structured data pipeline for training data extraction.
No intelligent document processing capability — documents stored as opaque files with basic metadata.
Simple document taxonomy exists (category field) that could seed an AI classification model.

priority_recommendations: Rewrite on a modern platform — Replace ColdFusion with a modern open-source framework, containerize, and deploy on AWS managed services
Migrate to a managed database — Move from self-managed SQL Server 2005 to Amazon RDS or Aurora with parameterized queries
Implement CI/CD and observability — Build automated pipelines, add testing, implement infrastructure as code, and instrument monitoring
Fix critical security vulnerabilities — Parameterize SQL, sanitize inputs, enforce HTTPS, implement proper authentication
Add analytics and AI capabilities — Integrate AWS analytics and AI services for intelligent document management
